title: Choose the visual world for GerminaWiki
question: The roll assigned Rede de Linhas (the São Paulo metro map as the wiki's map). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Rede de Linhas
options.lineage: São Paulo Metrô and CPTM wayfinding: numbered coloured lines, station diagrams, transfer signs
options.thesis: Every subject is a line, every page a station, every [[link]] a transfer: the wiki reads as the network students ride daily.
materials: Wikipedia serif headwords over a Helvetica-style UI
options.viewport: Article in a Libertinus Serif headword at full scale on white, a vertical line diagram of the subject's pages on the left with this station lit, the subject roundel in the title margin.
options.risk: If line colour leaks into text fields it turns into a theme park; colour must stay on edges, roundels and the diagram.

raised.raise: One reading size does the work: body fixed at a 64-character measure, H2s hang in the left margin on a line-colour tick.
Colour lives only on edges, roundels and the line diagram; the text field stays achromatic, like a sign panel.
State is a station mark, not a hue: filled station = here, ring = visited, struck = missing page, dashed = draft.
Neutrals come from one strict grey ramp; no ad-hoc greys anywhere in the app.
One element per viewport is allowed to be big enough to win: the page headword.

options.label: Caderno Universitário
options.lineage: the Brazilian spiral notebook: ruled lines, red margin rule, coloured section dividers
options.thesis: The wiki as the class's shared caderno: every subject a coloured divider, every page a ruled sheet you can write on.
options.viewport: Article on a ruled sheet with the red margin rule, headword written large, subject divider tabs stacked on the fore-edge.
options.risk: Familiar to the point of cliché; paper skeuomorphism slides quickly into childish or into the cream-and-serif look every generator ships.

options.label: Manual de Referência
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manuals with tabbed coloured divider boards
options.thesis: The wiki as a reference manual: a stepped tab rail per subject, acetate leaves over a full-colour section board.
options.viewport: Open manual: the subject's colour board behind an acetate article leaf, tab rail down the right edge sized by page count.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: subjects map to tabbed divisions and the measure discipline is excellent; loses on identification, students never held these manuals.
options.risk: The 90 ms stepped, no-easing motion contradicts the Notion-smooth feel you asked for.

options.label: Tempestade de Letras
options.thesis: Words condense into weather across a white field.
options.viewport: A single word-weather event per screen.
options.case: Fuses poorly: spectacle fights reading and editing.
options.kept: Headword set with real mass (tight, large), not as a timid title.

options.label: Borda Iridescente
options.thesis: Achromatic field with a hairline spectral edge.
options.viewport: Wide white margins, colour only on edges.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to students or school.
options.kept: Colour confined to edges; the text field stays achromatic.
options.risk: Pastel and faint on a projector.

options.label: Cartaz de Rua
options.thesis: Every square inch occupied; one calm white panel wins.
options.viewport: Full-bleed collage with one white panel.
options.case: Fuses poorly: you ruled out playful.
options.kept: One element per viewport big enough to win.

options.label: Mesa de Corte
options.thesis: Sections strung along a perforated rail.
options.viewport: A frame rail across a grain-orange field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dark and editorial-tool heavy.
options.kept: State as a mark, not a hue.

options.label: Ficha de Ampliação
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over a zone ramp.
options.kept: One strict grey ramp for every neutral.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern wiki done well: Wikipedia Vector-2022 reading with Notion's editor chrome.
canonCard.viewport: Familiar article layout, table of contents left, tools right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every wiki by design; exactly the 'literal Wikipedia clone' you flagged.
